design_rationale:
WORKLOG — auto_loan_payment_servicing / task 0 (root problem: auto_ext_due_day_realignment)

STEP 0. DRAW AND SCOPE.
scripts/draw_counts.py env/regional_retail_bank/tasks/auto_loan_payment_servicing --tasks 2 printed:
  {"task": 0, "prerequisite_problems": 3, "problems": 4, "factor_counts": [4, 5, 4, 6]}
  {"task": 1, "prerequisite_problems": 1, "problems": 2, "factor_counts": [5, 4]}
Task 0 is therefore a tree of four problems and the four drawn factor counts are assigned:
auto_ext_fee_overcharge_correction 4, auto_ext_call_payment_amount 6, auto_ext_autopay_rate_restatement 5,
auto_ext_due_day_realignment 4. Nothing was occupied before this task. This task claims four policies and
four task tools: correct_loan_fee_ab5fa380, post_installment_payment_1d25a699, set_loan_autopay_8313b066 and
change_payment_due_day_9dcc583e. Left for task 1 (two problems): the payoff settlement figure on a payment
tool of its own and the refund owed on coverage financed with a loan, neither of which any policy here
touches — this task claims no payoff, no coverage and no lien write, and its tools write only the fee
adjustment, the installment payment, the drafting instruction and the due day.

WHY IT MAKES A GOOD TEST. The caller asks for one small thing — her car payment day moved later. Nothing
she says points at a charge booked for too much, at the installment she has let slip, or at the standing
draft on the loan. All three come out of the published rules: the realignment rule says outright that the
day moves only once no standing draft instruction remains and only after the loan stands current; the
restatement rule says the rate is fixed only after every installment already due stands satisfied; the
payment rule says the amount is fixed only after every late charge carries the amount the charter fixes.
The agent has to walk that chain backwards to the charge, correct it, take the payment (which is the
borrower's own to make), have her withdraw the draft, and only then work out the day. Every hop changes a
number downstream, so an agent that discovers the chain but resolves it in the wrong order, or skips a
hop, writes different figures and fails on the terminal hash. The difficulty is in reading the policy and
reconciling the ledger, not in choosing between similar tools: each problem has exactly one write.

BASE-INVARIANT CARD.
- auto_fee_waiver (the correction write) is governed by auto_evt_fee_waiver alone. courtesy_count: the
  customer's courtesy late charge waivers in the rolling 365 days must be below late_charge_courtesy_waivers_365d
  (1 on this product) — the ledger carries no auto_fee_waiver row at all, so the count is 0, evidenced by the
  adjustment_reason on the January fee row. on_time_before: at least 6 consecutive on-time installments
  before the late one — the installments due 2026-03-03 through 2026-08-03 were all paid on the 1st of their
  month, six in a row. loan_open_for_courtesy: status active. waive_once: no waiver names this charge as its
  source; the correction's source_item_id is the charge's own reference. No time gate.
- auto_payment (the payment write) is governed by auto_evt_payment_allocation (loan_open: status active, and
  the payment is applied fees, then interest, then principal) and by auto_evt_payoff_and_lien, which fixes no
  gate reaching a scheduled installment payment, so it enters as policy_scope. No time gate.
- auto_set_autopay is governed by auto_evt_autopay (source_account: the drafting account must be a checking
  account of the same customer in active status — the Everyday Checking account 6318 is active and hers) and
  auto_agg_relationship_discount, which fixes no gate on the instruction write and enters as policy_scope.
- auto_change_due_date is governed by auto_due_date_change. once_a_year is a time gate: anchor
  auto_loans.last_due_date_change_date = 2024-05-21, duration params.due_date_change_window_days = 365,
  relation not_before, calendar days counted with the day after the change as day 1, boundary inclusive. The
  window closed 2025-05-21, 483 days before the frozen date, so the gate holds. Just-failing case: a change
  recorded 2025-09-17 would put the window's end at 2026-09-17, one day after the frozen date, and the
  correct conclusion would be to decline; just-passing case: a change recorded 2025-09-16 ends the window
  exactly on the frozen date and, the boundary being inclusive, allows it. current_and_active is judged at
  handling time, that is after the payment of step 11: status active and days_past_due 0. On the opening
  world it is false (days_past_due 13), which is precisely the design.

BUSINESS-OBJECT CARD. The target object of the correction is one ledger entry: the late charge posted
2026-09-14 for the installment due 2026-09-03, amount 31.25, unsettled. The correlation key written back is
source_item_id = that entry's own reference. Excluded: the late charge of 2026-01-14 (17.00), which was
settled in full by the payment of 2026-01-20 and is linked to it by an auto_fee_settlement row, and the
returned payment charge of 2026-08-14 (25.00), which is a different fee code linked to the returned
principal-only payment. The target of the payment is the installment due 2026-09-03, named in the
installment_due_date argument; earlier installments are excluded because each already carries a scheduled
payment credited to its own due date. The target of the instruction and the day change is the loan row.

PROBLEM-TREE CARD.
  root auto_ext_due_day_realignment
    <- auto_ext_autopay_rate_restatement   kind state_gate, gate auto_loans.autopay_enrolled, form state
    <- auto_ext_call_payment_amount        kind value_input, gate record_span, form state
  auto_ext_autopay_rate_restatement
    <- auto_ext_call_payment_amount        kind value_input, gate arrears_adjustment, form state
  auto_ext_call_payment_amount
    <- auto_ext_fee_overcharge_correction  kind value_input, gate charges_to_clear, form state
Three prerequisite problems, matching the draw; three of the four edges are value_input, above the floor of
max(3-1,1) = 2. Topological order: correction, payment, instruction, due day — forced and unique, because the
instruction waits on the payment and both wait, transitively, on the correction.
Four-point test on each prerequisite sentence:
 1. "The amount a payment taken during a call must cover is fixed only after every late charge standing on
    the loan carries the amount this charter fixes for it." Ordering connective "only after"; the waiting
    side is a record-visible state (what the late charge entries on the loan show against the charter
    amount); no tool, policy id or code token; the strength is a hard requirement and the scope is late
    charges standing on that loan, exactly the condition. Exactly one write in this difficulty brings that
    state about: only correct_loan_fee_ab5fa380 books an entry against a charge, and its own policy says so
    in its own words ("put right by one correction entry booked against that charge for the difference").
    Derivation: the reader sees a charge of 31.25, works the charter amount out as 17.00, sees the state
    fails, and finds the one policy whose write books the difference.
 2. "The rate restated on the loan is fixed only after every installment already due stands satisfied on the
    loan's records." Connective "only after"; record-visible state (the installments and the past-due count);
    no code names; hard requirement over installments already due. Exactly one write brings it about: only
    post_installment_payment_1d25a699 credits a payment toward an installment and returns the past-due count
    to zero.
 3. "A due day is moved only once no standing instruction to draft the installment from a deposit account
    remains on the loan." Connective "only once"; record-visible state (the loan shows a drafting
    instruction and the account it draws on); no code names; hard requirement. Exactly one write brings it
    about: only set_loan_autopay_8313b066 sets or withdraws that instruction.
 4. "The realigned day is settled only after the loan stands current with no installment past due on its
    records." Connective "only after"; record-visible state; no code names; hard requirement. Same single
    write as (2), and the two sentences are distinct in wording and neither contains the other.
No rule names another problem's tool or id, and no depended-on rule restates the sentence of the side that
waits on it. Seed evidence that each edge is false at the opening is recorded per edge in
prerequisite_closure.edges[].unresolved_at_frozen_time. Deletion sensitivity, from the Step 5 run:
skip the correction -> payment_amount 635.55 instead of 621.30; skip the payment -> restated_apr 8.20
instead of 8.15 and realigned_due_day 15 instead of 16; skip the instruction -> the loan still carries the
draft and its terminal row differs in four fields.

STEP 3. THE WORLD AND WHY EACH CLASS OF ROW IS THERE.
- customers: one profile, Rosalind Amaro, SC resident (the state whose grace days, 10, make a charge on the
  2026-09-03 installment due by 2026-09-14 and keep days_past_due at 13, under the 30 at which the loan would
  turn delinquent — both facts the tree needs).
- auto_loans: one Certified Pre-Owned Vehicle Loan, 60 months at 7.99 (7.24 base + 1.25 grade B - 0.50 of
  stacked reductions), monthly 576.30, due day 3, next due 2026-09-03 unsatisfied, autopay enrolled against
  the checking account, last due day change 2024-05-21. Remove the draft flag and edge 3 vanishes; move the
  next due date forward and edges 2 and 4 vanish; move the last due day change inside 365 days and the task
  becomes a refusal.
- auto_transactions, 41 rows: the funding disbursement; 34 scheduled installments whose splits are worked at
  7.99 on the principal then outstanding for the days since the previous credit, so the history teaches the
  charter's own arithmetic and not a rival one; the late charge of 2026-01-14 and the payment of 2026-01-20
  that settled it, which is what makes the twenty-four month late charge count 2 and so the ceiling 22.00
  rather than 15.40; a principal-only payment of 900.00 returned unpaid on 2026-08-14 with its reversal and
  the 25.00 returned payment charge, which is what keeps a second charge standing outside the current
  calendar month so that the charges-cleared window factor bites; and the overstated late charge of 31.25.
  Delete the January pair and the ceiling factor changes the answer; delete the returned payment pair and
  the charges-cleared window factor stops biting.
- checking_accounts / checking_transactions: Everyday Checking opened 2019-06-14, balance 1284.75 against the
  1500.00 waiver balance its tier publishes — deliberately just under, so every multi-source tier fails its
  first limb and passes on the deposits; three payroll deposits of 2410.55 and three rent debits of 1982.30,
  which are exactly the ledger the balance equals. The three deposits decide four tiers and their total,
  7231.65, is the deposit measure of the realignment.
- card_accounts / card_transactions: Cash Rewards Visa, limit 9000.00, balance 1240.00 (under a quarter of
  the limit, which anchors the payment clock), 18450 reward points (over the mid threshold, under the deep),
  14 purchases totalling 7180.40 over twelve months of which 10 fall in the last three
  (2026-06-28 onward, by 0 <= MONTHS(posted_date, 2026-09-16) < 3). The purchase of
  2025-10-09 is the near-miss: it sits 11 whole months back and counts toward the twelve-month total, while
  the payment of 2026-08-20 is not a purchase and a careless reader who counts it would push the
  three-month purchase count to 11 and still not reach the deep count of 12; the deep card thresholds of
  this policy set (9000.00, 12 purchases) are just out of reach on 7180.40 and 10, so every card tier lands
  on its middle rung rather than its top one.
- No cache field is used as a trap in this task, and no stamp names any factor's outcome: rate_discounts
  records what the rate carries, never which tier a factor selects.

FACTOR CARD (per policy: ladder tier taken, evidence, baseline reading, and the figure the baseline gives,
from the Step 5 sensitivity run; the whole-baseline fall-back is the last number in each line).
auto_ext_fee_overcharge_correction, result 14.25, whole baseline 15.85:

  acting_base_rule (method, checking): middle tier, balance 1284.75 under the 1500.00 waiver balance but

  standing, 632.55 -> 12.25.
  charge_ceiling_step (parameter): two late charges in twenty-four months -> ceiling 22.00, which does not
  bite; baseline ceiling 15.40, which does -> 16.25.
  charter_charge_rounding (method): 35 whole months on book -> rounded half-up to the whole dollar, 17.00;
  baseline half-up to the cent, 17.29 -> 13.96.
auto_ext_call_payment_amount, result 621.30, whole baseline 758.34:
  payment_interest_rate (parameter, card) middle tier -> 7.74; baseline 7.99 -> 622.30.
  accrual_clock_anchor (method, card) top tier on card utilisation -> clock from 2026-09-03, 13 days;
  baseline from the last payment credited, 46 days -> 716.30.
  accrual_endpoint_convention (method, checking) middle tier -> span counted as it stands; baseline adds a

  payment_interest_rounding (method) middle tier: the interest before rounding is 37.52,

auto_ext_autopay_rate_restatement, result 8.15, whole baseline 8.84:
  restored_draft_reduction (parameter, card) middle tier -> 0.15; baseline the published 0.25 -> 8.25.
  manual_payment_step_value (parameter, card) middle tier -> 0.05; baseline 0.10 -> 8.20.
  arrears_adjustment_method (method) top tier, the installment then due is 2026-10-03 after the payment ->

  standing_deposit_allowance (parameter, checking) middle tier -> 0.60 percent of 8.19 = 0.04914; baseline

  restated_rate_rounding (method) middle tier -> rounded up to the cent, 8.15; baseline half-up, 8.14.
auto_ext_due_day_realignment, result 16, whole baseline 12:
  realignment_base_shift (parameter, card) middle tier -> 5 days; baseline 3 -> day 14.
  record_credit_window (method) middle tier, 35 months on book -> installments of the last twenty-four
  months, 24 -> 4 days; baseline all 35 over the life of the loan -> day 17.
  deposit_credit_step (parameter, checking) middle tier -> 1.5; baseline 1.0 -> day 15.
  deposit_measure_aggregation (method, checking) middle tier, account 87 months old -> the three-month

Every declared factor moves the result, and every whole-baseline figure differs from gold, so an agent who
finds only a computation document computes a definite wrong number with no signal. Each computation carries
two cross-difficulty factors or more, two parameter factors or more and two method factors or more, and at
least two multi-source factors whose every tier beyond the fall-through combines two conditions over
distinct records.

INHERITANCE AND OVERRIDES. Nothing in base is quietly displaced; every sentence of base that this task's
policies reach a different number on is named in the overriding policy's own `overwrite`, clause by clause.
Five are declared across the four policies of this task:
 - auto_evt_late_charge's "The charge equals late_charge_pct_by_state percent of monthly_payment, rounded
   half-up to the cent, capped at late_charge_cap_by_state" -> the four-step method of the correction policy;
 - auto_evt_fee_waiver's "A fee is waived in full, never in part, as one auto_fee_waiver row whose
   source_item_id is the fee." -> the correction entry booked against the charge for the difference;
 - auto_evt_payment_allocation's "interest owed at any moment is auto_msr_accrued_interest, computed on the
   principal balance from last_payment_date" -> the call-payment policy's own interest sentence, which fixes
   the rate, the clock and the rounding of the interest a payment taken during a call must cover. This is the
   quantity auto_msr_accrued_interest measures; declaring it here is what retires the base reading of 137.06
   on this world and leaves 38.00 as the only interest the charter states for that payment;
 - auto_evt_autopay's "Enrolling adds the autopay discount to the APR ... on the same schedule when
   autopay_discount_removed_on_cancel is true." -> the restatement being written on the day the instruction
   changes;
 - auto_agg_relationship_discount's "When autopay is cancelled and autopay_discount_removed_on_cancel is
   true, the APR rises by the autopay discount actually applied, and re-enrolling later restores it" -> the
   restatement sentence that raises the recorded rate by the reduction restored, the arrears adjustment and
   the manual-payment step, less the standing deposit allowance. This is what retires the base reading of
   8.24 and leaves 8.15 as the only restated rate the charter states.
The clause granularity is deliberate: the same base sentence's remainder, "the relationship discount is
unaffected by autopay changes", is NOT superseded and is exactly what fixes rate_discounts at
"relationship" after the withdrawal. Every other base clause stands: the allocation order, the satisfaction
rule, the grace days, the one-charge-per-installment rule, the returned payment fee, the drafting account
rule, the once-per-window due date rule, the 1-to-28 day range and the maximum shift, the cap and the APR
floor, and every eligibility gate listed above.

STEP 5. VERIFICATION ACTUALLY RUN.
The builder replays the gold writes with the real tools onto the seeded DB and evaluates each policy's
compute on the world as it stands just before its own write, exactly as the gate does. Output:
  P1 correction_amount = 14.25   (acting_base 576.3, rate 3.0, ceiling 22.0, charter charge 17.0, standing 31.25, months 35)
  P2 payment_amount = 621.3      (charges_to_clear 17.0, allowance 10.0, component 7.0, interest 38.0, span 13, days 13, rate 7.74)
     split fees 42.0 / interest 38.0 / principal 541.3
  P3 restated_apr = 8.15         (raised 8.19, relief 0.15, step 0.05, arrears 0.0, allowance 0.04914)
  P4 realigned_due_day = 16      (base 5, span 24, credit 4.0, step 1.5, measure 7231.65, deposit credit 4.5, shift 13.5)
  factor sensitivity and whole-baseline figures as listed in the factor card above
  prerequisite sensitivity: skip P1 -> P2 = 635.55; skip P2 -> P3 = 8.2; skip P2 -> P4 = 15.0
These are the numbers written into computations.expected, factor_sensitivity and baseline_result.

DRAFT RECOMPUTATION FROM THE VISIBLE CONTEXT. Masking the extended yaml, the compute, the expected values
and this dossier, and working only from what a rollout sees — the published rules, the tool schemas, the
rows the finders return and what the caller actually says — the reading is: she wants the due day moved; the
realignment rule makes the day wait on a loan with no standing draft and no installment past due; the loan
row shows both false; the restatement rule makes the rate wait on the installments already due being
satisfied; the payment rule makes its amount wait on the late charges carrying the charter amount; the
ledger shows one late charge of 31.25 against a charter amount of 17.00. So: correct 14.25, take 621.30 from
the borrower split 42.00 / 38.00 / 541.30 against the installment due 2026-09-03 with the next due 2026-10-03,
have her withdraw the draft with the rate restated to 8.15 carrying the relationship reduction, then move the
day to the 16th with the next installment 2026-10-16. That is gold, reached without the hidden assets.

REACHABILITY IN ONE CONVERSATION. Every step is a synchronous write under one frozen_time. Nothing waits on
a real-world event: the money moves on the caller's debit card during the call, the instruction is her own
and takes effect at once, the correction and the day change are the bank's own book entries. No status
registration stands in for something happening outside the environment. Every question a real agent must ask
has an answer in the persona (identity, which loan, when the change should take effect, how she will pay,
whether she agrees to the draft coming off, and an explicit "I don't keep track" for anything she could not
know), and the two customer-side writes are handed over by the agent and run by her, their receipts entering
the shared transcript.

EASY MISTAKES AND HOW THE POLICY EXCLUDES THEM. Correcting the January charge instead of the September one
(the rule says the amount standing is the most recently assessed charge, and the January one was settled).
Computing the payment's interest from the last payment credited (the clock anchor tier moves it to the
installment then due because the card balance is under a quarter of the limit). Clearing every charge
standing in the payment amount (the charges-cleared window tier restricts it to the current calendar month
because only three charges were assessed in twelve months) — while the allocation of the payment does clear
all 42.00, which is a different question the rule answers separately. Restating the rate before taking the
payment (the arrears adjustment would add 0.05 and give 8.20). Moving the day before the payment (the record
credit would be 3 days and the day the 15th). Reading the checking balance as meeting the waiver balance
(1284.75 is under 1500.00, so every first limb fails and the middle tiers apply).

user_scenario:
Rosalind Amaro manages the front office of an orthopedic practice in Greenville, South Carolina, and she calls Piedmont Crescent on her break, talking fast because she has patients waiting. She opens with the one thing she wants: "I need to move my car payment to later in the month. I changed jobs in the spring and payroll hits on the 20th now, so the beginning of the month is always a scramble." She means the car loan she has with the bank on her Subaru, and she wants the new day to hold from the next payment onward, not some future cycle; she says so if the agent asks when she wants it to take effect. She is content for the representative to make whatever changes to the loan the bank's rules call for, and she says plainly that if something needs her own say-so she will do it herself while she is on the line.

She volunteers nothing else about the loan. Asked who she is, she gives her mobile number, 8645550547, and then, when asked for more, her date of birth, 1979-04-22, the last four of her Social, 1537, and the ZIP on her statements, 29605. Asked how she gets paid, she says a payroll deposit lands in her Piedmont Crescent checking account. Asked about her balances or what the loan is carrying, she says she genuinely does not keep track: "You have the records in front of you, I don't." If she is asked for a figure she cannot know, such as what interest has built up or what a charge should have been, she says she has no idea and leaves it to the representative.

Her cooperation is entirely reactive. If the representative tells her that a payment that has already come due has to be satisfied before the day can be moved, she does not argue: "Then let's get it paid. Take it on my debit card, I've got it right here." When the representative hands her the payment to make herself, she makes it for whatever figure she is told and reads back the confirmation she gets. If the representative explains that the loan cannot carry an automatic draft while the day is being moved, she answers, "Fine, take the automatic payment off the loan, I'll put it back on after it settles," and she completes that instruction herself when it is handed to her. If the representative tells her a charge on the loan was booked for more than it should have been and is being put right, she says, "Well, I'm glad somebody caught it," and nothing more. If the representative quotes her a figure that is far off what she is expecting, she will say it does not sound like what she has been paying and ask for it to be checked against the record, but she never says what the right figure is, because she does not know it.

Once the representative tells her the due day has been moved and states the day it now falls on, she is satisfied and closes the call warmly: "That's exactly what I needed, thank you." She does not ask for anything else, does not ask for a letter or a statement, and does not press for anything the representative has not raised. If the representative never mentions the past-due payment or the automatic draft, she does not raise them either; she simply waits to hear what has been done.

request_alignment.claim: The borrower asks for the day of the month her auto loan installment falls due to be moved later in the month, effective from the next installment.
evidence: user_scenario:I need to move my car payment to later in the month.

request_alignment.claim: She authorises the representative to make the changes the bank's rules require on the loan and to hand her anything that needs her own instruction.
evidence: user_scenario:She is content for the representative to make whatever changes to the loan the bank's rules call for

gold_actions.business_effect: One correction entry is booked against the late charge of 2026-09-14 for 14.25, and the loan's unpaid fee balance falls from 56.25 to 42.00.

request_binding.action_semantics: The ledger carries a late charge assessed above the amount this charter fixes for it, a debt-like state the bank owes back whether or not the borrower mentions it; the only action it selects is a correction entry booked against that charge. It is not a courtesy removal of a correctly assessed charge and it is not a payment.

discriminator.business_meaning: a late charge standing on the loan for more than the amount the charter fixes for it

stage_provenance.fact: The charge being corrected stands unpaid on the loan at the moment of the call, and the correction itself is completed on the spot by this write.

base_preconditions.condition: The customer's courtesy late charge waivers in the rolling 365 days, counted by auto_msr_late_charge_courtesy_365d across all of the customer's auto loans, must be below late_charge_courtesy_waivers_365d.
The installments immediately before the late one must show at least late_charge_courtesy_min_on_time consecutive on-time installments by auto_msr_on_time_streak.

evaluation_criteria.necessity: The charge standing on the loan, the count of charges in the last twelve months, the count of late charges in twenty-four months and the counts of scheduled installments in twelve and twenty-four months are all reconciled from these rows; without them neither the correction nor the payment nor the realignment can be worked out.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Read the borrower's checking account: its tier, status, posted balance and the date it was opened.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Read the borrower's credit card account: its status, credit limit, balance owed and unredeemed reward points.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: The clock anchor tier rests on the balance owed against the limit, and the charge allowance and manual-payment step tiers rest on the reward points.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Read the card ledger: every purchase posted over the last twelve months and the payment made against the card.
